questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Come hell or high water

options.text: Not ready to go on adventures
Tired of all kinds of dangers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'In spite of any obstacle.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Given Idiom: ***Come hell or high water*** means **in spite of any obstacle**.

 
 
• *Example: I've always managed to get into work **come hell or high water***.
 
 
 
• From the given options, the third option is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

 Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **Mistake Points__**

__
 
• We may think from the phrase "Come hell or high water" that it is all about afraid of the challenges, but the correct answer is option 3. So be careful while dealing with such questions.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• *The phrase originated in America around the mid-1800s and the earliest print reference is from 1882 in an Iowa newspaper, The Burlington Weekly Hawk-Eye. However, why hell or high water is referenced as obstacles, is not clear.*

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

Savita will deliver a speech on the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti.

options.text: On the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti a speech is being delivered by Savita.
On the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti a speech was delivered by Savita.
On the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti a speech will be delivered by Savita.
On the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti a speech is to be delivered by Savita.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**On the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti a speech will be delivered by Savita**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64e177b3c5c5cb81c12b3d5b5ddabaaf474cdad3d6098992ca6592786c8147d6.png] 

 
• In **Active Voice**, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
 
• In **Passive Voice**, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
• The given sentence is in the **active voice** and '**Savita**' is the **subject **and ''**on the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti**'' is the object.
 
• When we convert this sentence into a **passive voice**, the **subject 'Savita**' of the active voice **becomes **the **object**, the **object **''**on the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti''****becomes **the **subject**.
 
• The passive format **"'will + be + V3 (delivered)"** should be used.
 
• This is the active and passive voice **rule **for the **future simple tense.**

Hence, the correct answer is **option 3*.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/87c1a28e731fadd9279228c1cea2f8e988a3f790bf9ccc89c9b0f02c423b1609.png]

questions.solution:

__
 
• The word '**Idleness**' means an inclination not to do work or engage in activities.
 
• The synonyms of the word 'Idleness' are "lethargy, apathy, **sluggishness**".
 
• From the synonym of the given word, we can say that the word 'Lethargy' has the same meaning.
 
• The word 'Lethargy' means a lack of energy and enthusiasm.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 4. Let's see the meaning of other given options:-

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Out of bounds
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Forbidden.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Given Idiom: ***Out of bounds*** means forbidden; not allowed.

 
 
• *Example: The path by the railway line is officially **out of bounds** to both cyclists and walkers*.
 
 
 
• From the given options, the first option is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **Mistake Points__**

__
 
• We may think from the phrase "Out of bounds" that it means limitless, but the correct answer is option 1. So be careful while dealing with such questions.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• *This expression alludes to the boundaries of the playing area in numerous sports and to the rules applying to them. Its figurative use dates from the 1940s*.
